title: Asking your insurer to cover a wig
intro: Some insurers cover part or all of the cost of a wig for medical hair loss, under a different name. Rules differ by plan, so ask before you buy.

steps.text: Ask your insurer if they cover a "cranial prosthesis" or "hair prosthesis". Those are their names for a medical wig.
Ask your doctor for a prescription or letter using the wording your insurer asks for. Many insurers require one.
Keep the receipt for the wig, and fill in the insurer's claim form.
Medicare plans usually don't cover a wig for hair loss from chemotherapy. Medicare Advantage plans may differ, so ask your plan.
Keep a record of what you spend on medical costs each year, in case it helps at tax time.
Ask whether the insurer needs a billing code on the receipt, and whether they approve it before you buy.

sources.title: American Cancer Society: Choosing and wearing a wig

title: Asking your hospital for a wig
intro: Help with wig costs depends on your hospital and where in the UK you live.

steps.text: Ask your hospital's cancer information centre whether you can have a free wig or a voucher.
Some hospitals offer one free wig if treatment causes hair loss. Others work differently, so ask before you pay for one.
Macmillan's helpline can tell you about wigs, hats and scalp care.
